name: Air Fryer Chicken Katsu with Rice and Katsu Sauce

components.name: Chicken Katsu

ingredients.name: Raw chicken breast, sliced into even cutlets
Neutral oil for browning crumbs and spray

steps: Lightly toast panko in a skillet with some measured oil until golden; let cool. This follows the original baked-katsu technique, adapted for air frying.
Flatten chicken cutlets to a similar thickness, season, dust in flour, dip in egg, then firmly coat with golden panko.
Preheat air fryer to 190 C. Place cutlets in a single layer with a little remaining oil spray; cook approximately 12-15 minutes, flipping halfway, until 74 C in the centre.

components.name: Short Grain Rice
steps: Cook rice with the listed water and rest it covered. Whisk ketchup, Worcestershire, soy and honey into a dipping sauce.

components.name: Katsu Sauce & Slaw
steps: Finely shred cabbage and carrot and store separately. Divide katsu and rice across five meals; re-crisp chicken in air fryer before eating and add raw slaw and sauce cold.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Air fryer variation supported by Just One Cookbook guidance for its baked katsu; source is not an original dedicated air fryer formula.
Planning: Secondary skillet for toasting crumbs and stovetop for rice. Sauce is measured UNHANGRY formulation.
Freezer: cooked crumbed chicken and rice freeze; crust softens; slaw fresh
Dietary: Wheat, egg, soy; Worcestershire may contain fish.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (≤4°C); refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers, freeze portions for later in the week, and reheat to at least 74°C.
